It covers the setup for audience insights, attribution tracking, growth and churn analysis, UI/UX optimization, content discovery, and custom event tracking. The document provides detailed instructions on initializing the analytics plugin, tracking various user interactions, and ingesting necessary data models to unlock features like churn prediction and personalized content recommendations. It also includes code snippets and parameter definitions for implementing tracking methods, ensuring developers can effectively integrate analytics capabilities to enhance user experience and inform marketing strategies.

616280.name: iOS Product Analytics Data Ingestion Requirements.md
616280.description: The file "iOS Product Analytics Data Ingestion Requirements.md" outlines the necessary data ingestion specifications for integrating Product Analytics modules within an iOS platform. It details the requirements for audience and content analytics, including correct user identifier integration, content catalog model ingestion, and the setup of related data tables such as Electronic Program Guide and Channel Catalog. The document provides a comprehensive guide on the dimensions and data types needed to gain insights into viewer demographics, content performance, and engagement, enabling tailored content strategies and optimization of content offerings for iOS applications.

616284.name: iOS App Analytics Integration.md
616284.description: Title: iOS App Analytics Integration Guide Description: This document outlines two approaches for integrating App Analytics into iOS applications: Simple Integration Workflow and Advanced Integration Workflow. The Simple Workflow allows clients to track app performance without managing sessions, using `begin()` and `end()` functions for session management. The Advanced Workflow provides more control, exposing functions like `fireSessionStart()`, `forceNewSession()`, `fireNav()`, `fireEvent()`, and `fireSessionStop()` for detailed session and event tracking. The guide includes code examples in Swift and Objective-C for various analytics events, including app crashes, app errors, UI errors, login results, signup results, and TV pair results. It also introduces new events for API result logging and error handling, with detailed descriptions of required metrics and dimensions for accurate analytics. This comprehensive guide is designed to help developers effectively monitor and improve app performance by leveraging App Analytics features.

616292.name: iOS Advanced Integration.md
616292.description: The `iOS Advanced Integration.md` file provides detailed guidance on advanced integration techniques for the NpawPlugin in iOS applications. It covers manual lifecycle management of the plugin, allowing for greater control over initialization and destruction of the `NpawPlugin` instance. Developers can create and manage the plugin instance using a builder pattern and should manually handle the instance's lifecycle to prevent memory leaks. The file also explains how to introspect adapter states within the plugin to understand their current conditions, which is essential for determining the values of metrics and the appropriateness of firing certain events. Additionally, it describes how to switch adapters on a `VideoAdapter`, enabling the reassignment of player and ad adapters at runtime, and how to manually fire events before dedicated adapters are instantiated. A significant section is dedicated to modifying request parameters using the `WillSendRequestListener` for both `VideoAdapter` and `AppAnalytics` components, allowing dynamic changes to metadata and other request parameters. Finally, the document discusses how to delay the `/start` event until all desired metadata is available, ensuring accurate tracking and analytics. It also provides instructions on injecting custom data into external tables using the `fireEvent` function. In summary, this file is a comprehensive resource for iOS developers looking to implement advanced integration features of the NpawPlugin, offering enhanced flexibility and control over plugin behavior, event tracking, and data management.

616296.name: iOS Video Adapter Example Integrations.md
616296.description: Title: iOS Video Adapter Example Integrations Description: This document provides a guide on integrating video playback using AVPlayer with the NpawPlugin for iOS. It includes example code in Swift and Objective-C for a common integration flow, handling channel changes, and managing video termination to ensure accurate analytics reporting. The examples demonstrate how to set up a video player, change video sources, and properly conclude video sessions with the NpawPlugin for a seamless user experience.

616300.name: iOS Enable Debug.md
616300.description: Title: iOS Enable Debug.md Description: This document provides instructions for enabling debug-level console logging in the NPAW Plugin for iOS. It details how to set different logging levels, including silent, error, warning, notice, debug, and verbose, using an enumeration in Swift and Objective-C. The file includes code snippets demonstrating how to initialize the plugin with a specified log level, specifically setting it to debug mode for more detailed output during development and troubleshooting. This guide is essential for developers needing to adjust logging verbosity for better insight into the plugin's operations on iOS devices.

616304.name: iOS CDN Detection.md
616304.description: Title: iOS CDN Detection Guide Description: This document outlines the CDN detection process for iOS applications, detailing how to enable and customize CDN parsing for video content. It covers enabling CDN detection, prioritizing URLs for parsing, handling CDN responses, and managing a list of recognized CDNs. Additionally, it provides instructions for detecting custom CDNs by reading headers or implementing custom parsing logic, including examples. The guide also explains how to parse manifests for DASH and HLS streams, handle authentication, and manually set transport stream formats. This resource is essential for developers integrating CDN detection into their iOS video streaming applications to monitor and optimize content delivery performance.

616308.name: iOS Custom Video Events.md
616308.description: Title: iOS Custom Video Events.md Description: This document provides guidance on firing custom video events in iOS applications using a plugin. It includes Swift and Objective-C code examples for sending custom events with dimensions and metrics to analytics suites, and explains how to send data to external tables using the `fireEvent` method. The file is a resource for developers looking to track and analyze custom video interactions within their iOS apps.

616312.name: iOS Custom Video Adapter.md
616312.description: The `iOS Custom Video Adapter.md` file provides a comprehensive guide on implementing a custom video adapter for iOS using the `PlayerAdapter<AnyObject>` class from an iOS library. It details the standard video playback flow, including start, pause, resume, seek, buffer, and stop events, and outlines the required and optional data to be tracked during video playback, such as live status, player name, resource, and rendition details. The document also includes example Swift code for creating a custom adapter for AVPlayer and Bitmovin players, demonstrating how to register and unregister listeners, handle playback state changes, and manage error handling. This guide is essential for developers looking to integrate advanced video tracking features into their iOS applications.

616316.name: iOS Custom Ads Adapter.md
616316.description: Title: iOS Custom Ads Adapter Guide Description: This document provides a comprehensive guide on implementing a custom ads adapter for iOS using the `AdAdapter<AdPlayer>` class. It outlines the ad flow events, required and optional data points for ad analytics tracking, and methods for integrating the adapter with an iOS video player. Developers will learn how to handle ad events, register listeners, and provide necessary ad playback information to ensure proper ad tracking and analytics. The guide includes code examples and instructions for integrating the custom adapter with the NPAW plugin for a seamless advertising experience within iOS applications.

616320.name: iOS Multiple Players.md
616320.description: The "iOS Multiple Players.md" file provides guidance on managing multiple video players in an iOS application using a specialized library. It explains how to use unique identifiers to segregate video adapters for different content types, such as main content and advertisements, ensuring isolated management and preventing resource conflicts. The document includes Swift code examples for initializing video adapters with identifiers and details a smart destruction mechanism that maintains a single instance per identifier for efficient resource handling. This approach allows for seamless integration and control of multiple video players within dynamic application contexts.

616324.name: iOS Offline Events.md
616324.description: The "iOS Offline Events.md" file provides guidance on implementing offline event tracking for iOS applications using the NPAW Plugin. It explains how to enable offline mode for capturing video events when users download content for offline viewing, and how to temporarily store these events locally to be sent to NPAW servers once internet connectivity is restored. The document outlines limitations, such as the inability to switch between online and offline modes after plugin initialization, the lack of support for app analytics events in offline mode, and the 30-day event processing limit. It also notes the unavailability of offline mode for tvOS due to its lack of a reliable local storage mechanism. The file includes code snippets for enabling offline events and instructions on how to send stored offline events, with attention to constraints and proper initialization procedures.

616332.name: iOS Plugin Options Analytics.md
616332.description: The `iOS Plugin Options Analytics.md` file provides a comprehensive guide on customizing analytics for the NPAW plugin within iOS applications. It outlines how to inject an `AnalyticsOptions` object to personalize analytics data, including app name, release version, network information, device details, ad metadata, user information, and other advanced features. The document also covers setting custom dimensions and integrating with video options, with code examples in Swift and Objective-C. This guide is essential for iOS developers looking to tailor the analytics plugin to fit their specific needs and enhance the quality of data collected for performance monitoring and user experience analysis.

616336.name: iOS Plugin Options Video.md
616336.description: The `iOS Plugin Options Video.md` file provides comprehensive documentation on how to personalize the NPAW (Nice People At Work) plugin for iOS applications. This file serves as a guide for developers to set various video and ad metadata options, which are crucial for analytics and tracking purposes within the NPAW Suite. The file outlines how to create a `VideoOptions` object, populate it with detailed video content information such as title, program, duration, and live status, and associate it with an `AVPlayer` instance using the NPAW plugin. It also covers how to set metadata for ads, including titles, campaigns, and expected ad patterns. Additionally, the documentation explains advanced features like CDN node parsing, manifest parsing, handling live content, and custom dimensions for more granular analytics. Developers can specify up to 20 custom dimensions to filter data based on specific criteria like content sections or user demographics. The guide emphasizes the ability to dynamically update certain values in real-time, allowing for more accurate and timely analytics data. This dynamic updating capability is subject to activation upon request to NPAW support. In summary, this file is an essential resource for iOS developers integrating the NPAW analytics plugin into their video streaming applications, providing them with the tools to capture rich data for performance monitoring and user experience optimization.

616340.name: iOS Plugin Options Balancer.md
616340.description: Title: iOS Plugin Options Balancer.md Description: This comprehensive guide details how to personalize the NPAW CDN Balancer for iOS applications by injecting a `BalancerOptions` object during NPAW Plugin initialization. It outlines various customization options such as profile and bucket selection, live content flagging, P2P video identification, decision call forcing, domain whitelisting, dynamic rule application, and balancing of audio, subtitles, and manifests. Additionally, it covers JWT authentication setup for API calls. The document includes code snippets in Swift and Objective-C for implementing these configurations, ensuring optimized content delivery and enhanced user experience on iOS devices.

616344.name: iOS Migrate From Plugin v7.1.md
616344.description: Title: iOS Migrate From Plugin 7.1.md Description: This guide outlines the key changes when upgrading from NPAW Plugin v7.1 to v7.2 for iOS, including dependency management updates, import statement modifications, and plugin initialization adjustments. It serves as a reference for developers to ensure a smooth transition to the latest plugin version. (198 characters)

616348.name: iOS Migrate From Plugin v6.md
616348.description: Title: iOS Migration Guide from Youbora Plugin v6 to NPAW Plugin v7.2 Description: This document outlines the key differences between Youbora Plugin v6 and NPAW Plugin v7.2 for iOS, providing a step-by-step guide for migrating to the newer plugin version. It covers managing dependencies, updating import statements, setting analytics options, initializing the plugin using a singleton pattern or builder, integrating the plugin with a video player, and utilizing the updated App Analytics features. The guide includes code samples for replacing old plugin references, handling content URLs, and firing player and app events to ensure a smooth transition to the latest NPAW Plugin functionalities.

616356.name: NPAW Plugin Integration Out-of-the-Box Metrics and Dimensions.md
616356.description: The "NPAW Plugin Integration Out-of-the-Box.md" file provides a comprehensive list of pre-configured metrics and dimensions for video analytics, enabling users to monitor and analyze video performance, user engagement, and quality of experience. It details over 50 metrics such as Unique Users, Plays vs Completion Rate, Bandwidth, and Error tracking, along with dimensions like Play Head, Country, Device, and Connection Type, to facilitate data filtering and insights for optimizing video delivery and user satisfaction.

616360.name: NPAW Plugin Integration Custom Metrics and Dimensions.md
616360.description: Title: NPAW Plugin Integration Custom Metrics and Dimensions Guide Description: This guide provides instructions for integrating custom metrics and dimensions with the NPAW Plugin. It covers the benefits of tracking user interactions with custom events, how to register and implement custom metrics (including aggregation types and limitations), and how to create and use custom dimensions for more tailored data analysis. The document also includes code examples for setting up custom metrics and dimensions within the NPAW Suite, emphasizing the importance of pre-registration with backend teams to ensure proper data classification and storage.

616364.name: NPAW Plugin Integration Balancer Metrics and Dimensions.md
616364.description: The "NPAW Plugin Integration Balancer Metrics and Dimensions.md" file provides an extensive list of metrics and dimensions for monitoring and analyzing the performance of Multi CDN and P2P video delivery systems. It details various performance indicators such as chunk counts, byte volumes, response times, cache hits/misses, error rates, and throughput, along with dimensions that categorize data by user, device, application, content, geography, and CDN balancer configurations. This comprehensive set of data points enables users to assess the efficiency of content delivery, troubleshoot issues, and optimize the viewer experience across different platforms and networks.

616368.name: NPAW Plugin Integration Balancer API Metrics and Dimensions.md
616368.description: The "NPAW Plugin Integration Balancer API Metrics and Dimensions.md" file provides detailed information on the key performance indicators (KPIs) and filtering options available within the NPAW (Nice People At Work) Plugin Integration for Balancer API. It outlines various metrics such as API error rates, response counts, average and extreme response times, which are crucial for monitoring API reliability and performance. Additionally, the file lists dimensions that allow users to segment data based on user and device info, application and player details, content metadata, geographical location, and CDN balancer configurations. This enables comprehensive analysis of streaming video performance and user experience across different parameters.

616376.name: NPAW Plugin Integration Standalone Balancer.md
616376.description: The "NPAW Plugin Integration Standalone Balancer.md" file provides integration guides for adding NPAW's CDN Balancer support to legacy v6 plugins across various platforms, including JS (Web), Android, and iOS, without requiring a full plugin rewrite. It enables maintainance of existing v6 integrations while extending functionality to include the CDN Balancer component for improved video delivery performance.

616392.name: JavaScript Standalone Balancer.md
616392.description: The "JavaScript Standalone Balancer.md" file provides documentation for integrating the CDN Balancer Plugin SDK with web applications using various video players like Shaka, Bitmovin, THEOplayer, and Video.js. It covers installation via NPM or direct script inclusion, prerequisites, initialization with account details, optional P2P module integration, customization options for CDN balancing, and instructions for destroying the plugin instance if needed. The guide is tailored for both general web apps and specific SmartTV platforms, ensuring flexible implementation for developers.

616396.name: JavaScript Standalone Balancer Bitmovin.md
616396.description: The file "JavaScript Standalone Balancer Bitmovin.md" provides guidance on integrating the CDN Balancer SDK with web applications using the Bitmovin player. It includes setup instructions, a note on compatibility with SmartTV platforms, a warning about limitations with Safari browser, and the necessary JavaScript configuration for the Bitmovin player to work with the CDN Balancer Plugin. Users are instructed to contact their Customer Engineer for the adapter URL. After integration, metrics will be visible in the NPAW Suite dashboards.

616400.name: JavaScript Standalone Balancer Shaka.md
616400.description: Title: JavaScript Standalone Balancer Shaka.md Description: This markdown file provides guidance on integrating the CDN Balancer Plugin SDK with web applications using the Shaka player, particularly for SmartTVs on Tizen (Samsung) and WebOS (LG) platforms. It includes a code snippet for setting the networking engine to capture player requests and mentions the visibility of metrics in NPAW Suite dashboards post-integration.

616404.name: JavaScript Standalone Balancer THEOplayer.md
616404.description: Title: JavaScript Standalone Balancer THEOplayer.md Description: This document provides instructions for integrating the CDN Balancer Plugin SDK with web applications using THEOplayer versions 5.x.x, 4.x.x, and 3.x.x. It outlines the steps to set the manifest URL and add an interceptor to THEOplayer for enhanced content delivery network performance, with integration completion indicated by metrics display in NPAW Suite dashboards.

616408.name: Android Standalone Balancer.md
616408.description: The `Android Standalone Balancer.md` file provides documentation for integrating the NPAW CDN Balancer Plugin into Android applications using various video players like Media3 ExoPlayer, Exoplayer, and Bitmovin. It outlines the prerequisites, installation steps, plugin lifecycle management, and advanced integration techniques. The guide includes code examples in both Java and Kotlin for initializing, using, and destroying the plugin instance to ensure optimal performance and avoid memory leaks. It also details how to enable optional P2P and Bolina service support. This documentation is essential for Android developers looking to implement adaptive streaming solutions for improved video delivery quality.

616412.name: Android Standalone Balancer Bitmovin.md
616412.description: Title: Android Standalone Balancer Bitmovin Guide Description: This document provides instructions for integrating the CDN Balancer Plugin with Bitmovin Android player versions 3.4.0 to 3.48.0. It ensures compatibility with the legacy v6 Bitmovin Adapter from version 6.8.1 and above. The guide includes steps to install the player adapter via Gradle and demonstrates how to integrate the balancer plugin with the player using both Java and Kotlin code snippets. It also covers customizing an existing `NetworkConfig` with the balancer for advanced configurations. This guide is essential for Android developers looking to optimize content delivery and streaming performance in their Bitmovin-based applications.

616416.name: Android Standalone Balancer ExoPlayer.md
616416.description: Title: Android Standalone Balancer ExoPlayer Guide Description: This guide provides instructions for integrating the CDN Balancer Plugin with ExoPlayer on Android for versions 2.19.1 to 2.14.x. It covers compatibility with the legacy v6 Exoplayer Adapter, installation of the player adapter, and advanced integration techniques, including custom ExoPlayer dependencies, MediaSourceFactory configurations, custom headers, cache management, and using a custom OkHttpClient for network requests. Essential for developers looking to optimize media streaming with load balancing capabilities.

616420.name: Android Standalone Balancer Media3 ExoPlayer.md
616420.description: The "Android Standalone Balancer Media3 ExoPlayer.md" file provides a technical guide on integrating the CDN Balancer Plugin with Media3 ExoPlayer in Android applications. It covers compatibility with legacy v6 Media3 ExoPlayer Adapter, installation instructions for the player adapter, and detailed steps for integrating the CDN Balancer Plugin with the ExoPlayer. The document also includes advanced integration techniques, such as handling custom Media3 ExoPlayer dependencies, creating custom MediaSource.Factory with headers, and using a custom OkHttpClient for network requests. This guide is essential for Android developers looking to optimize media streaming performance using the CDN Balancer Plugin with Media3 ExoPlayer versions 1.3.1 to 1.0.x.

616424.name: iOS Standalone Balancer.md
616424.description: The `iOS Standalone Balancer.md` file provides detailed instructions for integrating the CDN Balancer Plugin iOS SDK into an iOS application. It covers prerequisites, installation methods using Swift Package Manager and Cocoapods, plugin lifecycle management, and advanced integration techniques. The guide explains how to initialize the plugin with an account code, manage its lifecycle, and inject legacy plugins. It targets developers looking to optimize video streaming performance within their iOS apps by using the NPAW (Nice People At Work) plugin. The document is essential for developers who need to implement a content delivery network (CDN) balancing solution to ensure efficient and high-quality video delivery to end-users.

616432.name: NPAW Plugin Integration Certification Tool.md
616432.description: The NPAW Plugin Integration Certification Tool.md file describes a self-certifying diagnostic tool for verifying the integration of the NPAW plugin within applications. It checks CDN Balancer functionality, video and ads analytics event transmission, and provides results post-plugin creation or video playback end. The tool ensures proper interception of requests, data access, and event capturing, aiding in seamless plugin integration.

616436.name: NPAW Plugin Integration JavaScript Certification Tool.md
616436.description: The "NPAW Plugin Integration JavaScript Certification Tool.md" file provides documentation for a JavaScript-based diagnostic tool used to analyze the performance of NPAW (Nice People At Work) plugins within web applications. It outlines local configuration settings for CDN balancer, video analytics, and ads analytics diagnostics, and demonstrates how to generate and view performance reports in the browser's developer console. The tool helps ensure successful integration and functionality of NPAW's performance optimization and analytics features for streaming video content and advertisements.

616440.name: NPAW Plugin Integration Android Certification Tool.md
616440.description: The NPAW Plugin Integration Android Certification Tool file provides instructions and code snippets for integrating and certifying the NPAW (Nice People At Work) plugin within Android applications. It outlines how to set diagnostic options for CDN Balancer, Video Player Analytics, and Ad Analytics, and how to trigger and view diagnostic reports using the NPAW plugin. The tool ensures proper integration and functionality of the plugin's features by generating detailed certification reports, which can be accessed via Android Logcat. This documentation is essential for Android developers looking to validate the performance and analytics capabilities of their video streaming applications.

616444.name: NPAW Plugin Integration iOS Certification Tool.md
616444.description: The "NPAW Plugin Integration iOS Certification Tool.md" file provides guidance on configuring and running the NPAW (Nice People At Work) diagnostic tool for iOS to certify plugin integrations. It outlines Swift code snippets for setting diagnostic options such as CDN balancer, video analytics, and ad analytics, and demonstrates how to generate and access diagnostic reports within XCode's Debug Area. The file also includes an example of the diagnostic tool's output, showcasing successful integration and event tracking for CDN balancer, video player analytics, and ad analytics. This resource is essential for developers integrating NPAW's analytics plugins into iOS applications to ensure proper functionality and data collection.

616452.name: NPAW Plugin Integration FTP Data Ingestion Procedure.md
616452.description: "This document outlines the FTP data ingestion procedure for integrating the NPAW Plugin. It provides step-by-step instructions for advanced users to securely upload and correlate data to the NPAW Suite using FTP. It includes connection details, directory creation guidelines, and post-upload data access methods via API or NPAW Suite dashboards."

616456.name: NPAW Plugin Integration How to Avoid Ad Blockers.md
616456.description: Title: NPAW Plugin Integration: Bypassing Ad Blockers with CNAME Configuration Description: This guide provides step-by-step instructions for integrating the NPAW (Nice People At Work) plugin to circumvent ad blockers by setting up a CNAME in your DNS. It outlines how to maintain tracking of customer data for both HTTP and HTTPS sites by configuring your domain to point to NPAW's beaconing domains, ensuring analytics continuity. The document also covers certificate management for HTTPS traffic and custom plugin initialization parameters for advanced configuration, with support available from NPAW's Customer Engineers and Support team.

616460.name: NPAW Plugin Integration Playhead Tracker API.md
616460.description: The NPAW Plugin Integration Playhead Tracker API.md file provides documentation for an API that tracks a user's playback position in a video player. It includes a JavaScript library example that demonstrates how to retrieve the playhead position using the API, allowing for seamless video playback resumption and performance analysis. The API requires an account code and provides methods to fetch the playhead data, which can be used to enhance user experience by enabling video content to start from where the user last stopped watching.

616464.name: NPAW Plugin Integration Share Blocker.md
616464.description: The "NPAW Plugin Integration Share Blocker.md" file provides a guide for integrating the Share Blocker feature into video players using NPAW (Nice People At Work) plugins. It outlines steps for configuring access controls to limit concurrent streams and IP connections, ensuring compliance with account sharing policies. The document includes instructions for setting up profiles, integrating the Share Blocker API, and dynamically updating profiles, along with a JavaScript example for implementing a check against concurrency limits. This integration is crucial for content providers to manage and restrict unauthorized account sharing.

616500.name: /{accountCode}/decision.md
616500.description: The `/{accountCode}/decision.md` file provides documentation for an API endpoint used to retrieve a list of recommended CDNs for content delivery based on a default user profile. It outlines the API request format, including required and optional query parameters for customizing the CDN selection process, such as resource path, bucket group, user IP, user agent, content type, and security features like token authentication. The file also details the structure of the API response, including possible status codes and error messages. This guide helps users understand how to interact with the API to optimize content delivery through NPAW's CDN Balancer service.

616504.name: /{accountCode}/{profile}/decision.md
616504.description: The `decision.md` file provides documentation for an API endpoint used to retrieve a list of recommended Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) for a specific user profile within the NPAW platform. It outlines the necessary path and query parameters, including authentication mechanisms for secure access, and details the request and response structures, including error codes. The endpoint supports both live and video-on-demand (VoD) content delivery optimization, with optional parameters for enhanced customization and security, such as dynamic traffic allocation rules and token-based authentication. This resource is essential for developers integrating CDN selection functionality into their applications to improve media streaming performance and reliability.

616556.name: Setting up a CDN Profile.md
616556.description: Title: Setting up a CDN Profile.md Description: This guide provides a step-by-step process for configuring a CDN profile within the CDN Balancer system. It covers creating and naming profiles, setting general information and security rules, and adding provider rules for custom CDN configurations. The document also explains how to apply specific rules for different user types and how to use the default profile if conditions are not met. It is intended for advanced users who require an in-depth understanding of CDN setup for data-driven optimization of content delivery, enhancing user experience. System integration is a prerequisite for the API and CDN Balancer app to function correctly.

616560.name: Adding a CDN Provider.md
616560.description: Title: Adding a CDN Provider Configuration Guide Description: This guide provides step-by-step instructions for configuring a Content Delivery Network (CDN) provider within a CDN balancer profile. It covers the creation of a new profile, setting general information, adding provider rules, configuring security rules, and managing traffic distribution through weight calibration and performance thresholds. The document also explains how to use the multidimensional matrix for rule-based traffic routing, including country-specific access controls. It's an essential resource for optimizing CDN performance and managing costs effectively.

616564.name: CDN Security Rules and Configuration.md
616564.description: The "CDN Security Rules and Configuration.md" file provides guidance on securing a CDN by configuring security and provider rules. It explains the difference in scope between security rules, which affect all CDN requests, and provider rules, which allow or deny specific CDNs. The document details how to access security settings and outlines the use of country, device, IP range, and token tabs to control access and enhance security for CDN services. It includes step-by-step instructions and use cases for implementing these rules to tailor CDN balancing to specific needs, such as geo-blocking, device restriction, IP whitelisting, and token-based security.

616568.name: CDN Advanced Rules.md
616568.description: "CDN Advanced Rules.md" contains instructions for configuring advanced rulesets in a CDN Balancer for network, business, and performance optimization. It details how to set up filters for traffic based on dimensions like country, ISP, and device, and metrics such as bandwidth and error rates. The document also explains how to assign weights and prices for Round-Robin load balancing strategies, ensuring efficient content delivery and improved user experience.

616572.name: DNS Based CDN Balancer.md
616572.description: "DNS Based CDN Balancer.md" outlines NPAW's solution for optimizing content delivery by automatically directing users to the best-performing CDN in real-time. It details the easy integration process, the benefits of DNS-level balancing for enhanced streaming quality, and the rules applied to ensure optimal content distribution. The file also discusses DNS protocol limitations and the technical setup required for DNS delegation to NPAW's servers for efficient CDN balancing.

616576.name: CDN IP Logging.md
616576.description: "CDN IP Logging.md" outlines the process for enhancing NPAW Suite's load balancing algorithm by integrating real-time data collection from supported CDNs (Fastly, Akamai, CloudFront, Lumen). It provides setup instructions, required API parameters for each CDN, and details on accessing CDN Traffic Volume data via external API connections. This guide helps users leverage their CDN data for improved network performance and traffic management.

616768.name: NPAW Device Probe.md
616768.description: The NPAW Device Probe (NDP) is a tool for automated video monitoring and quality assurance, offering real-time analytics, event detection, and centralized control for enhanced troubleshooting and integration with external systems. It features continuous monitoring, fast root cause identification, and extensive scripting capabilities for QA testing, with a customizable dashboard for comprehensive analysis and workflow automation. NDP streamlines video QA processes and integrates seamlessly with third-party platforms, improving video engineer productivity and ensuring optimal end-user experiences.

616772.name: NDP Getting Started.md
616772.description: The "NDP Getting Started.md" file provides a comprehensive guide on setting up and using the NPAW (Nice People At Work) Device Probe (NDP) for monitoring and analyzing video streaming performance on various devices such as set-top boxes, Android and iOS mobiles, and personal computers. It covers hardware specifications for portable and rackmount options, installation instructions, device connection diagrams, and steps to verify the installation and operation of the NDP. The guide also includes troubleshooting tips for ensuring proper connectivity and interaction with the devices being tested, as well as instructions for installing necessary certificates for HTTPS sniffing. Users are guided on how to access the NDP Manager for remote management and monitoring of the probes. The document is essential for new users to quickly get started with deploying and using the NDP system effectively.

616804.name: NDP Manager.md
616804.description: The `NDP Manager.md` file is a documentation guide for the NPAW Device Probes management platform, known as NDP Manager. It serves as a centralized access point for monitoring and managing NPAW probes across various customer sites. The document outlines the login process, account management, password security policies, and the integration capabilities with third-party solutions like Grafana, Kibana, and SNMP Network Management systems. It details the functionalities of the NDP Manager, including user account management, probe monitoring, dashboard creation, asset management, coordination of monitoring routines, and admin operations. The platform ensures secure access, data persistence, and real-time monitoring of key performance indicators (KPIs) for video streaming services. It also provides instructions for configuring network layouts for high performance and availability, and for integrating with external systems for enhanced data visualization and network management.

616808.name: NDP Admin Area.md
616808.description: The "NDP Admin Area.md" file provides comprehensive documentation on the Admin Area of the NDP Manager, detailing how users with admin or superadmin roles can manage dashboards, users, probes, and groups. It outlines the capabilities and restrictions for each user type, the process for creating and editing user accounts, and the advanced actions available for probe management and group configurations. This guide serves as a key resource for NDP Manager administrators to effectively oversee and control the system's operations and user permissions.

616812.name: NDP REST API.md
616812.description: The "NDP REST API.md" file provides documentation for integrating the NPAW Video Device Probe with various software development and management tools via a RESTful HTTP API. It covers content-type requirements, resources pagination, authentication using API keys, and authorization mechanisms. The API supports easy integration with CI/CD pipelines, test management, ticketing systems like Jenkins, Watson, JIRA, and GIT, and is documented following the Swagger/OpenAPI specification. The file includes details on how to obtain and use session tokens for secure access to probe resources.

616816.name: NDP Widgets.md
616816.description: The "NDP Widgets.md" file provides a comprehensive guide to the NPAW Device Probe (NDP) dashboard widgets. 617763.name: Sending Player Errors v6.md
617763.description: Title: Sending Player Errors v6.md Description: This document outlines the process for reporting and handling player errors within the NPAW Suite. 617771.name: Setting Options, Dimensions, and Metadata v6.md
617771.description: The "Setting Options, Dimensions, and Metadata v6.md" file provides comprehensive documentation for integrating NPAW Suite Analytics into applications. 617779.name: SSO Integration v6.md
617779.description: Title: SSO Integration v6.md Description: This document provides a comprehensive guide on integrating Single Sign-On (SSO) with NPAW Suite using version 6 of the SSO protocol. The file outlines the necessary steps for configuring SSO through SAML and OpenID Connect, including specific setup details for each supported IdP, ensuring a secure and seamless authentication experience across the NPAW Suite platform.

617783.name: SAML v6.md
617783.description: Title: SAML v6 Configuration and Role Management Guide Description: This document outlines the implementation of Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) v6 for managing user access, roles, and account permissions within the NPAW Suite. It provides detailed instructions on configuring basic access with essential SAML attributes (email and role), as well as advanced role and permission management using specific SAML attribute assertions (account_permissions). The guide includes XML examples for SAML responses, explains how to create the account_permissions claim in Azure AD, and covers additional features such as populating user profile fields (firstName and lastName) via SAML attributes. It also details the necessary steps to configure Microsoft Graph API permissions and client credentials for integrating with Azure AD. This file is essential for IT administrators setting up SAML-based Single Sign-On (SSO) for secure and efficient user management in the NPAW Suite environment.

617787.name: iOS Nagra.md

The document also notes the absence of Google IMA ads integration for Nagra on iOS and points to further customization options for video metadata and other parameters. This resource is essential for developers looking to implement advanced video analytics in their iOS/tvOS applications with Nagra support.
